17-2.title: ACCOUNTANT, PUBLIC
17-2.description: Persons shall be deemed to be in practice as public accountants within the meaning and intent of the Act who either individually, as members of a partnership or limited liability company or as officers of a corporation, sign, affix or associate their names or any trade or assumed names used by them in a profession or business to any report expressing or disclaiming an opinion on a financial statement based on an audit or examination of that statement, or expressing assurance on a financial statement.
17-2.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

00-78.title: Enrolled Actuary
00-78.description: Enrolled Actuaries meet experience requirements and pass an examination. EAs are experts on the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA). The EA designation is awarded by the Joint Board for the Enrollment of Actuaries, located at the Internal Revenue Service, U.S. Department of the Treasury. Renewal every 3 years requires continuing actuarial education and other professional development activities. For detailed information, see http://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-utl/20cfr901.pdf or http://www.irs.gov/taxpros/actuaries/index.html.
00-78.agency: U.S. Department of the Treasury · Joint Board for the Enrollment of Actuaries

17-122.title: ENGINEER, INTERN
17-122.description: An individual who is enrolled as an engineer intern as a result of qualifying by education and examination.
17-122.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-124.title: ENGINEER, PROFESSIONAL
17-124.description: An individual who, through the knowledge of mathematical and natural sciences, applies judgment to the materials and forces of nature for the planning and design of engineering works and systems which include transportation facilities, sewage facilities, waterway improvement, refrigeration systems, air conditioning, electrical energy facilities, mineral extraction and refining facilities, and chemical processing and production facilities.
17-124.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

00-18.title: Air Traffic Control Tower Operator
00-18.description: Requirements to obtain an Air Traffic Control Tower Operator certificate include passing a written test. Besides the basic certificate, to act at any operating position, the individual must pass a practical test on control tower equipment and its use. To obtain a facility rating, the individual must have at least six months experience and pass another practical test. This certificate is valid until surrendered, suspended or revoked, although the individual must maintain current experience to work under the certificate. Detailed information can be found at web sites:http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ, http://www.natca.org/assets/Documents/mediacenter/controller_brochure.pdf, http://www2.faa.gov/careers/employment/atc.htm, and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.31-65.50.

00-12.title: Aircraft Mechanic - A & P
00-12.description: Aircraft mechanics are certified by the FAA with either an airframe (A) or powerplant (P) rating. Initial ratings require either completion of FAA Approved Aviation Maintenance Technician School or 18 months of work experience. Applicants must pass written, oral and practical exams. Thirty months of work experience is required for a combined Airframe & Powerplant (A & P) certificate. To obtain an inspector's authorization, a mechanic must have held an A & P certificate for at least 3 years. This certificate is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked, but requires currency of experience or refresher training. For further information, go the web site of the Veterans Employment and Training Service (VETS): http://umet-vets.dol.gov/airframe-mechanic.htm, http://www1.faa.gov/AVR/afs/mechanics.htm, and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.71-65.95.

00-16.title: Aircraft Repairer
00-16.description: To be eligible for a repairman certificate, a person must have the qualifications needed on the job. These qualifications may be obtained through 18 months of work experience or completion of formal training. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://www2.faa.gov/education/rlib/career.htm and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.101-65.105.

00-02.title: Airline Transport Pilot
00-02.description: To become certified (licensed) as an Airline Transport Pilot (ATP), an individual must have a Commercial Pilot certificate or equivalent with an instrument rating for airplane, helicopter, or powered-lift (glider). Air flight training and ground school as well as flight experience are requirements. They also must pass a strict physical examination and have 20/20 vision with or without glasses, good hearing, and no physical handicaps that could impair performance. They must pass a written test and a demonstration of flying ability. This license is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked; but the pilot must have a current medical certificate. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.151-61.167.

00-08.title: Commercial Pilot
00-08.description: All pilots who are paid to transport passengers or cargo must have a Commercial Pilot's license with an instrument rating issued by the FAA. To qualify for this license, the applicant must be at least 18 years old and have at least 250 hours of flight experience. The time can be reduced through participation in certain flight school curricula approved by the FAA. The individual also must pass a strict physical examination and have 20/20 vision with or without glasses, good hearing, and no physical handicaps that could impair performance. Passing a written test and a demonstration of flying ability are required. This license is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked; but the pilot must have a current medical certificate. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.121-61.133 and http://www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf.

00-15.title: Flight Engineer
00-15.description: To become certified as a Flight Engineer requires that the individual have either training or experience. Passing a written exam and a practical test and having a current medical certificate are also required. This certificate is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked. Detailed information can be found on the web sites: http://umet-vets.dol.gov/flightengineer.htm and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr63_00.html, parts 63.31-63.43.

00-77.title: Flight Instructor
00-77.description: To obtain certification as a Flight Instructor, the individual must hold either a Commercial Pilot or Airline Transport Pilot certificate with appropriate aircraft and instrument ratings. Training is required as well as experience in the type of aircraft being rated. This license is valid for 2 years and may be renewed by one of several options, such as passing a practical test, documenting student success, or taking a refresher course. More details can be found at web sites: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.181-61.199, www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf, and http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ.

00-20.title: Flight Navigator
00-20.description: To become certified as a Flight Navigator, the individual must be at least 21 years old and have a medical certificate. He or she must have both training in flight navigation and practical experience. Passing written and practical tests are required as well as having a current medical certificate. This certificate is valid until surrendered, suspended, or revoked. Detailed information can be found on the web site: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr63_00.html, parts 63.51-63.61.

00-13.title: Ground Instructor
00-13.description: To obtain certification as a Ground Instructor, the individual must pass an aircraft navigation knowledge test and a test of the fundamentals of instructing, unless the person already is employed as a teacher or holds a teacher's certification. Detailed information can be found at web sites: http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ and http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.211-61.217.

requirements.label: Certification
requirements.value: Certification my substitute for license requirements

00-06.title: Private Pilot
00-06.description: Obtaining a Private Pilot certificate (license) requires the individual to complete ground and flight training, have flight experience, obtain a medical certificate, and pass a written exam as well as a demonstration of flying ability. This license is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked; but the pilot must have a current medical certificate. The FAA Advisory Circular, AC 61-12M, Student Pilot Guide, outlines general procedures for obtaining student and private pilot certificates. Detailed information can be found at web sites: http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr61_00.html, parts 61.102-61.117, and http://www.faa.gov/avr/afs/acs/61-65d.pdf.

17-115.title: EMD - EMERGENCY MEDICAL DISPATCHER
17-115.description: A person who accepts calls from the public for emergency medical services and dispatches designated medical services personnel and vehicles.

00-60.title: Medical Doctor
00-60.description: A ship's Medical Doctor is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A medical doctor must also hold a valid license as a physician or surgeon issued within the United States. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-60.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

17-277.title: LICENSED PHYSICIAN AND SURGEON
17-277.description: An individual licensed under the Medical Practice Act to practice medicine in all of its branches.
17-277.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-278.title: PHYSICIAN - LIMITED MEDICALTEMPORARY PERMIT
17-278.description: An individual holding a degree of Doctor of Medicine and persons holding the degree of Doctor of Osteopathy, or persons who have satisfied the requirement and are eligible to receive such a degree from a medical or osteopathic school, who wish to pursue programs of graduate training in this state, may receive without examination, at the discretion of the Department of Professional Regulation, a 6-month temporary license.
17-278.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-279.title: PHYSICIAN - TEMPORARY MEDICAL PERMIT
17-279.description: An individual holding a degree of Doctor of Medicine and persons holding the degree of Doctor of Osteopathy, or persons who have satisfied the requirement and are eligible to receive such degree from a medical or osteopathic school, who wish to pursue programs of graduate training in this state, may receive without examination, at the discretion of the Department of Professional Regulation, a 3-year temporary license.
17-279.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-281.title: VISITING PHYSICIAN PROFESSOR
17-281.description: An individual who maintains an equivalent authorization in his/her native licensing jurisdiction during the period of the visiting professor permit to practice medicine in all of its branches and has received a faculty appointment as a visiting professor in Illinois.
17-281.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-397.title: VISITING RESIDENT PERMIT
17-397.description: An individual who has been invited or appointed to perform a portion of a postgraduate clinical training program in an Illinois patient care clinic facility, and who has applied to the department at least 60 days prior to the commencement date of the training.
17-397.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-33.title: BLACKSMITH FARRIER
17-33.description: A farrier works with horses but needs training in blacksmithing in order to make the shoe properly.

17-131.title: EXERCISE PERSON
17-131.description: An individual who gallops or exercises the horse on the track each morning.

17-158.title: GROOM
17-158.description: Any person responsible for practical care of the horse: feeding, grooming, cleaning stalls, and attending to its general care.

17-219.title: HOTWALKER
17-219.description: Any person who walks a horse to cool him out after a race or workout.

17-288.title: PONY PERSON
17-288.description: A person who leads the horses to the paddock in the afternoon for the races and may provide exercise for a horse in the morning when a trainer does not want him exercised with a rider on his back.

17-21.title: ASSISTANT TRAINER
17-21.description: An individual who provides assistance to the horse trainer, usually in a larger stable where there are many horses to care for and train.

17-502.title: OWNER
17-502.description: An individual who owns, in whole or in part, or leases a horse eligible to race at the race meeting where the applicant seeks to participate.

17-256.title: OWNER/ASSISTANT TRAINER
17-256.description: An individual who owns, in whole or in part, or leases a horse eligible to race at the race meeting where the applicant seeks to participate. Capable of providing assistance to the trainer and meeting the financial obligations incurred in the ownership, stabling, racing, training, and care of a race horse.

17-503.title: OWNER/TRAINER
17-503.description: An individual who owns, in whole or in part, or leases a horse eligible to race at the race meeting where the applicant seeks to participate. Capable of providing assistance to the trainer and meeting the financial obligations incurred in the ownership, stabling, racing, training, and care of a race horse.

17-107.title: OWNER/TRAINER/DRIVER
17-107.description: A person who is both a driver and a trainer as well as an owner in the horse racing industry. Drives a standard bred (harness) horse; trains and enters horses to race at a race meeting; hires grooms, hotwalkers, exercise riders, pony persons, other trainers, veterinarians and blacksmiths.

17-373.title: TRAINER
17-373.description: A person who trains and enters horses to race for one or more owners and who is responsible for hiring grooms, hotwalkers, exercise riders, pony persons, assistant trainers, veterinarians and blacksmiths.

17-10.title: ARCHITECT
17-10.description: An individual who furnishes professional services in connection with the design and construction of any private or public building, building structure, building project, or addition to or alteration or restoration thereof. Applicants who have never taken any divisions of the A.R.E. should contact NCARB for eligibility to take the A.R.E.
17-10.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

00-48.title: Second Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-48.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Second Assistant Engineer - Upper Level, the applicant must, while holding a license as a Third Assistant Engineer, complete one of the following: 360 days of service as an Assistant Engineer; or a minimum of 180 days as an Assistant Engineer and 360 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED); or 360 days as Chief Engineer (Limited-Oceans). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-48.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-38.title: Second Mate - Upper Level
00-38.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Second Mate Upper Level requires 360 days service as Officer in Charge of a Navigational Watch (OIC) on ocean steam or motor vessels while licensed as a Third Mate. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Detailed information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-38.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

17-180.title: APPRENTICE JOCKEY
17-180.description: An individual who has entered into a contract with an owner or trainer or has been issued an apprentice certificate to ride in races. Has the ability to break a horse from a starting gate in company with other horses and under the observation of the starter.

17-178.title: JOCKEY
17-178.description: A professional race rider of thoroughbred horses who maneuvers for an advantageous position in relation to the other horses in the race.

17-24.title: ATHLETIC TRAINER
17-24.description: An individual who, under the direction of a team and/or consulting physician, carries out the practice of preventive and emergency care and physical reconditioning of injuries incurred by athletes participating in an athletic program, or a person who, under the direction of a physician, carries out comparable functions for health organization-based extramural programs of athletic training services. Duties include counseling on nutrition and hygiene; supervising the selection, fitting, and maintenance of protective equipment; assisting the coaching staff in the development and implementation of a conditioning program; and providing on-site injury care and evaluation.
17-24.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-25.title: AUDIOLOGIST
17-25.description: An individual who is trained to apply non-medical methods and procedures in the identification, measurement, testing, appraisal, prediction, habilitation, rehabilitation, or instruction related to hearing and the disorders of hearing. The practice of audiology includes any tasks, procedures or act that is necessary for evaluation, hearing or vestibular function.
17-25.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-351.title: SPEECH-LANGUAGE PATHOLOGIST
17-351.description: An individual who is trained to and who engages in speech-language pathology through the application of non-medical methods and procedures for the identification, measurement, testing, appraisal, prediction, habilitation, rehabilitation, and modification related to communication development, disorder, or disabilities of speech language, voice, swallowing, and other speech, language and voice related disorders.
17-351.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-312.title: REPAIRER
17-312.description: Any person in the business of returning a vehicle, other than a vehicle for which a salvage certificate has been issued, back to its original or operating condition by restoring, mending, straightening, replacing, altering, or painting its essential parts.

17-28.title: AUTOMOTIVE PARTS RECYCLER
17-28.description: An individual in the business of acquiring previously owned vehicles and vehicle parts for the primary purpose of disposing the parts of vehicles.

17-304.title: REBUILDER
17-304.description: Any person in the business of returning a vehicle, for which a salvage certificate has been previously issued, back to its original or operating condition.

17-472.title: REPAIRER LICENSES
17-472.description: A person who reapairs automotive parts is required to obtain a Repairer, Rebuilder, Automotive Parts Recycler, Scrap Processor or Auctioneer license from the Illinois Sec of State.

00-65.title: Ship Radar Endorsement
00-65.description: The Ship Radar Endorsement is issued by the Federal Communications Commission to licensed commercial radio operators. This endorsement allows them to repair, maintain, or internally adjust ship radar equipment. Passing a written exam is required. For further information, see the FCC web site at http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/sre.html.

17-29.title: BARBER
17-29.description: An individual who, through the application of preparations and the use of mechanical devices, performs personal services such as shaving or trimming the beard; facial and scalp treatment with oils, creams, or other preparations; cutting hair, hair styling, arranging, dressing, curling, waving and other hair services; and massage or treatment of the face and scalp.
17-29.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-81.title: COSMETOLOGIST
17-81.description: An individual who, for cosmetic or beautifying purposes, performs various services upon the hair such as dressing, cutting, bleaching, curling and chemical restructuring. Performs any practice of epilation or depilation of any person or any practice of beautifying, massaging, cleansing, exfoliating the stratum corneum of the epidermis, or stimulating the skin of the human body, including body treatments, body wraps, or the use of hydrotherapy. Applies makeup or eyelashes to any persons, tints eyebrows and eyelids, lightens hair on the body, and removes superfluous hair from the body by the use of depilatories, waxing, or tweezers. A cosmetologist may also provide manicures, pedicures, and apply artificial nails.
17-81.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-57.title: LICENSED ELECTROLOGIST
17-57.description: A person who specialize in permanently removing unwanted hair using electrolysis, a process that involves inserting an electric current into hair follicles with a fine needle.
17-57.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-174.title: INTERTRACK EMPLOYEE
17-174.description: An employee of an intertrack wagering facility.

00-21.title: FIRST Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T1
00-21.description: FIRST Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T1) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. Further information can be found at the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-24.title: General Radiotelephone Operator License - PG
00-24.description: General Radiotelephone Operator License (PG) is issued for a lifetime and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-26.title: GMDSS Radio Maintainer's License - DM
00-26.description: GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) Radio Maintainer's License (DM) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-27.title: GMDSS Radio Operator's License - DO
00-27.description: GMDSS (Global Maritime Distress and Safety System) Radio Operator's License (DO) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-25.title: Marine Radio Operator Permit - MP
00-25.description: Marine Radio Operator Permit (MP) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-58.title: Radio Officer
00-58.description: The Radio Officer's license is issued to applicants who have a valid Federal Communications Commission (FCC) license as first or second class radiotelegraph operator (T1, T2). Certain officers are required to hold Global Maritime Distress and Safety System (GMDSS) certification issued by the FCC. Further information can be found at theUSCG website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-58.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-75.title: Restricted Radiotelephone Operator Permit (RP)
00-75.description: RP holders are authorized to operate most aircraft and aeronautical ground stations. They can also operate marine radiotelephone stations aboard pleasure craft (other than those carrying more than six passengers for hire on the Great Lakes or bays or tidewaters or in the open sea) when operator licensing is required. To obtain this permit, you must be able to speak and hear; and keep a written log; and be familiar with provisions of applicable treaties, laws and rules which govern the radio station you will operate. For further information, see the Federal Communications web site at http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/rp.html.

00-22.title: SECOND Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T2
00-22.description: SECOND Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T2) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-23.title: THIRD Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate - T3
00-23.description: THIRD Class Radiotelegraph Operator's Certificate (T3) is issued for 5 years and requires one year of relevant experience and passing a written exam. For further information, go to the FCC web site: http://wireless.fcc.gov/commoperators/#QUAL6M.

00-57.title: Assistant Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels
00-57.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as an Assistant Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels include 1,080 days at sea with 720 days on Motor Vessels. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-57.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-56.title: Chief Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels
00-56.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Engineer - Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels include 1,440 days at sea with 360 days as a Licensed Engineer and 950 days on Motor Vessels. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm.
00-56.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-19.title: Inspector's Authorization
00-19.description: To obtain an inspector's authorization, a mechanic must have held an Aircraft Mechanic A & P certificate for at least 3 years. For further information, see web site http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ, parts 65.91-65.95.

00-41.title: Operator of Uninspected Passenger Vessels - OUPV
00-41.description: To become licensed as an Operator of Uninspected Passenger Vessels requires specific experience -- Near Coastal or Inland as well as passing a written exam. Recent training in First Aid and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) is also required. For complete details see the USCG web page http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr13_02, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at website http://frwebgate4.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/waisgate.cgi?WAISdocID=50846230377+3+0+0&WAISaction=retrieve or http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-41.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-42.title: Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels - OUTV
00-42.description: To become licensed as a an Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels (OUTV) or 2nd Class Operator of Uninspected Towing Vessels (OUTV) requires specific experience - Oceans (Domestic Route), Near Coastal or Inland, as well as passing a written exam. Recent training in First Aid and Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) is also required. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Details can be found on the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-42.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

17-15.title: ASBESTOS INSPECTOR
17-15.description: An individual licensed by the department to perform asbestos inspections for asbestos containing building materials in accordance with the Illinois Asbestos Abatement Act, the Illinois Commercial and Public Building Asbestos Abatement Act and Code.
17-15.agency: Illinois Department of Public Health Division of Environmental Health · Illinois Department of Public Health Division of Environmental Health

17-16.title: ASBESTOS MANAGEMENT PLANNER
17-16.description: An individual licensed by the department to prepare asbestos management plans pursuant to the Illinois Asbestos Abatement Act and Code for schools (kindergarten through 12th grade).
17-16.agency: Illinois Department of Public Health Division of Environmental Health · Illinois Department of Public Health Division of Environmental Health

17-17.title: ASBESTOS PROJECT DESIGNER
17-17.description: Any individual licensed by the department to design response actions for asbestos abatement pursuant to the Illinois Asbestos Abatement Act, the Illinois Commercial and Public Building Act and Code.
17-17.agency: Illinois Department of Public Health Division of Environmental Health · Illinois Department of Public Health Division of Environmental Health

17-19.title: ASBESTOS PROJECT SUPERVISOR
17-19.description: An individual licensed by the department designated as the licensed contractor's representative who is responsible for the on-site supervision of the removal, encapsulation, or enclosure of asbestos-containing building materials pursuant to the Illinois Asbestos Abatement Act, the Illinois Commercial and Public Building Act and Code.
17-19.agency: Illinois Department of Public Health Division of Environmental Health · Illinois Department of Public Health Division of Environmental Health

17-38.title: BOILER INSPECTOR, DEPUTY
17-38.description: An individual who inspects boilers and pressure vessels to assure safety in regards to installation, operation, and repairs.

17-87.title: CROSS-CONNECTION/CONTROL DEVICE INSPECTOR
17-87.description: An individual who inspects and tests in-line backflow assemblies, such as the double check, double detector check, reduced pressure principle, and reduced pressure principle detector assembly units which are installed to protect the potable water system from contamination due to backflow.

17-39.title: DEPUTY BOILER INSPECTOR, SPECIAL
17-39.description: An individual who inspects boilers and pressure vessels to assure safety in regards to installation, operation, and repairs for authorized insurance companies.

17-56.title: LICENSED HOME INSPECTOR
17-56.description: A person who is responsible for examining a home to identify any potential issues or problems that may exist.
17-56.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-337.title: SHAFT AND SLOPE EXAMINER
17-337.description: An individual who examines and inspects the initial construction or major construction of shaft and slope mine work pertaining to the health and safety of shaft and slope workers. Responsible for the varied on-shift and pre-shift inspections.
17-337.agency: Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training

17-74.title: COMMERCIAL DRIVER (TRUCK AND BUS OPERATOR)
17-74.description: An individual who operates a vehicle that is over 26,000 lbs. (single unit or combination unit) and is designed to transport property or sixteen or more passengers.
17-74.agency: Illinois Secretary of State Department of Driver Services · Commercial Driver Training Section

17-cdl.title: Commercial Drivers License (CDL)
17-cdl.description: Commercial Drivers Licenses are issued by state departments but are similar from state to state, since the minimum requirements of the licenses and endorsements are set centrally. For more information contact the state DMV or https://cms.fmcsa.dot.gov/registration/commercial-drivers-license/how-do-i-get-commercial-drivers-license.

17-Perfus.title: Perfusion
17-Perfus.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-88.title: DANCE STUDIO OWNER
17-88.description: Any person or business entity which contracts with members of the general public to provide dance studio services. Studios must register with the Secretary of State if they receive advance payments of $50.00 or more per month.
17-88.agency: Illinois Secretary of State Index Department

17-68.title: CHIROPRACTOR
17-68.description: An individual who treats human ailments without the use of drugs and without operative surgery.
17-68.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-69.title: CHIROPRACTOR VISITING PROFESSOR
17-69.description: An individual who maintains an equivalent authorization in his/her native licensing jurisdiction during the period of the visiting professor permit to practice the treatment of human ailments without the use of drugs and without operative surgery and has received a faculty appointment to teach in a chiropractic school in Illinois.
17-69.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-125.title: ENGINEER, STRUCTURAL
17-125.description: An individual engaged in the designing or supervising of the construction, enlargement or alteration of structures.
17-125.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-123.title: STRUCTURAL ENGINEERING INTERN
17-123.description: An individual who is enrolled as a structural engineer intern as a result of qualifying by education and examination.
17-123.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-228.title: INSURANCE ADJUSTER, PUBLIC
17-228.description: Any person engaged in the business of adjusting insurance claims. Represents an insured individual for compensation and, while representing that insured, either negotiates values, damages, or depreciation by applying the loss circumstances to insurance policy provisions.

17-229.title: INSURANCE PRODUCER
17-229.description: An individual who solicits, negotiates, effects, procures, renews, continues, or binds policies of insurance covering property or risks in Illinois.

17-411.title: SURPLUS LINES PRODUCER
17-411.description: A person who deals with insurance placed with unauthorized insurers through surplus line agents or producers.

17-367.title: THIRD PARTY ADMINISTRATOR
17-367.description: Any person who, on behalf of a plan sponsor or insurer, receives or collects charges, contributions or premiums for, or adjusts or settles claims on residents of this state in connection with any type of life or accident or health benefit.

17-368.title: THIRD PARTY CERTIFICATION LICENSE
17-368.description: Any person who conducts a qualified third party certification program pursuant to chapter 95 1/2, section 6-508 providing behind the wheel testing for driver's license applicants.
17-368.agency: Illinois Secretary of State Department of Driver Services · Commercial Driver Training Section

17-369.title: THIRD PARTY CERTIFYING ENTITY LICENSE
17-369.description: Any person, firm, association, partnership, or corporation licensed by the state to conduct a qualified third party certification program providing behind the wheel testing for driver's license applicants who are employees of the entity.
17-369.agency: Illinois Secretary of State Department of Driver Services · Commercial Driver Training Section

17-370.title: THIRD PARTY SAFETY OFFICER
17-370.description: Any individual employed by a third party entity licensed to conduct skills tests required by the Illinois Secretary of State for those applicants who are employed by the third party entity.
17-370.agency: Illinois Secretary of State Department of Driver Services · Commercial Driver Training Section

17-393.title: VIATICAL SETTLEMENT PROVIDER
17-393.description: An individual, partnership, corporation or other entity that enters into an agreement with a person who owns a life insurance policy, insuring the life of a person who has a catastrophic or life threatening illness or condition, to compensate for less than the expected death benefit of the insurance policy, in return for the policy owner's assignment, transfer, sale, devise or bequest of the death benefit or ownership of the insurance policy.

17-260.title: PASSENGER BOAT/CHARTER BOAT OPERATOR
17-260.description: An individual engaged in operating a boat that carries passengers for hire. Must obtain a passenger license (i.e. fishing guide).

17-293.title: PROCESSED WILD GAME FOOD DEALER
17-293.description: An individual engaged in the buying, selling or processing of wild game.

17-20.title: ASBESTOS WORKER
17-20.description: An individual who cleans, removes, encapsulates, encloses, hauls, or disposes of asbestos-containing building materials pursuant to the Illinois Asbestos Abatement Act, the Illinois Commercial and Public Building Act and Code.
17-20.agency: Illinois Department of Public Health Division of Environmental Health · Illinois Department of Public Health Division of Environmental Health

17-18.title: ASBESTOS PROJECT MANAGER
17-18.description: An individual licensed by the department and designated as the building owner's representative and is responsible for overseeing asbestos abatement activities pursuant to the Illinois Asbestos Abatement Act for schools (kindergarten through 12th grade).
17-18.agency: Illinois Department of Public Health Division of Environmental Health · Illinois Department of Public Health Division of Environmental Health

17-455.title: CLOSED LOOP WELL CONTRACTOR
17-455.description: A person who constructs wells or installs water wells are Licensed Water Well Contractors with Closed Loop Certification to ensure the safety of water supplies.

17-419.title: INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR SUPERVISOR
17-419.description: Self-employed individuals who perform many of the same functions as a regular employee. However, they typically work on an assignment basis and are not tied to one employer.
17-419.agency: Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training

17-462.title: INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR SUPERVISOR
17-462.description: A person who oversees the construction activities that take place on the worksite. They are heavily involved in planning, organizing and controlling projects and are responsible for supervising the contractors and staff while maintaining a safe work environment.

17-501.title: FOREMAN
17-501.description: A person who is in charge of daily operations in a harness or thoroughbred racing stable.

17-418.title: GENERAL SURFACE SUPERVISOR
17-418.description: Someone who Supervises and coordinates activities of workers engaged in operating equipment to move personnel, machinery, and supplies to various levels of underground mine.
17-418.agency: Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training

17-461.title: GENERAL SURFACE SUPERVISOR
17-461.description: A person who supervises and coordinates activities of workers engaged in operating equipment to move personnel, machinery, and supplies to various levels of underground mine.

17-210.title: MINE MANAGER
17-210.description: An individual who manages the day to day activities of the mine, plans the long range operational needs of the mine, and is responsible for the health and safety of the workers at a coal mine.
17-210.agency: Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training

17-338.title: SHAFT AND SLOPE SUPERVISOR
17-338.description: An individual who supervises the construction work activities during initial or major shaft and slope mine construction. Must be present in shaft and slope work areas at all times when work is in progress.
17-338.agency: Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training

17-339.title: SHAFT AND SLOPE WORKER
17-339.description: An individual who is involved with initial or major shaft and slope work during mine construction.
17-339.agency: Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training

17-146.title: STABLE - FOREMAN
17-146.description: Any person who works directly under the supervision of the head trainer. Responsible for the operation of the stable, feed time, stall upkeep, equipment upkeep, and blacksmith appointments. Oversees the hotwalker, caretakers, etc.

17-354.title: STATE MINE INSPECTOR
17-354.description: A person who performs technical and safety inspections of coal mines. Enforces compliance with the Coal Mining Act. Advises and discusses health and safety issues with mine operators. Assists mine operators and labor regarding safety matters.
17-354.agency: Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training

17-358.title: SURFACE MINE SUPERVISOR
17-358.description: A person who supervises all work activities in the following surface mining areas: overburden, drilling and shooting, pit coal loading and reclamation. This individual is directly responsible for the surface work activities at a coal mine.
17-358.agency: Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training

17-377.title: UNDERGROUND SHOT FIRER
17-377.description: An individual responsible for the handling procedures and safe detonation of explosives, while they are being used in an underground area of a coal mine.
17-377.agency: Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training

17-340.title: CERTIFIED SHORTHAND REPORTER
17-340.description: An individual who provides reporting services by means of manual or mechanical shorthand writing of grand jury, court or court-related proceedings in pre-trial examinations, examination, depositions, motions and related proceedings of like character or in proceedings of an administrative agency that is subject to judicial review.
17-340.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-341.title: RESTRICTED SHORTHAND REPORTER
17-341.description: An individual who is licensed, upon the written request of the Director of the Administrative Offices of the Illinois Courts, and appointed, in counties of less than 100,000 people, to engage in reporting only those court proceedings to which he/she may be assigned by the chief judge of his/her circuit.
17-341.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-420.title: CRANE HOIST OPERATOR
17-420.description: Someone responsible for operating a stationary or traveling crane to lift, move, position, and reposition loads. Depresses buttons, lifts levers, and ensures load is safely attached to crane before bringing it down.
17-420.agency: Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training

17-30.title: BARBER TEACHER
17-30.description: An individual who trains others in the practice and theory of barbering, which includes the application of preparations and use of mechanical devices to perform personal services such as shaving or trimming the beard; giving facials, scalp massages or treatment with oils; and cutting hair, styling, arranging, dressing, curling, cleaning, coloring and other similar work on the hair. The individual may also practice as a barber.
17-30.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-128.title: ESTHETICIAN TEACHER
17-128.description: An individual who provides instruction in the theory and practice of esthetics to students in a cosmetology or barber school approved to teach esthetics or an approved esthetics school, and who is authorized to practice as an esthetician.
17-128.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-362.title: TEACHER, PROVISIONAL CAREER & TECHNICAL
17-362.description: An individual who teaches children in a vocational education program.
17-362.agency: Dept. of Teacher Educ. and Certification · Illinois State Board of Education

17-364.title: TEACHER, SUBSTITUTE
17-364.description: A replacement teacher for an elementary or secondary teacher under contract on a day-to-day or short-term basis.
17-364.agency: Dept. of Teacher Educ. and Certification · Illinois State Board of Education

17-365.title: TEACHER, TRANSITIONAL BILINGUAL
17-365.description: An individual who teaches children in a transitional bilingual education program in grades K-12 in public school programs.
17-365.agency: Dept. of Teacher Educ. and Certification · Illinois State Board of Education

17-91.title: DENTAL HYGIENIST
17-91.description: An individual who, under the supervision of a dentist, is engaged in helping people prevent tooth decay and gum disease and maintain oral health. The person examines teeth and gums, cleans deposits and stains from teeth, and treats teeth with fluorides and other decay preventive agents. A dental hygienist takes impressions of teeth and removes sutures, temporary crowns, and restorations. May also take and develop X-rays and perform dental health education functions.
17-91.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-92.title: DENTAL SPECIALIST
17-92.description: An individual currently licensed as a dentist in Illinois who is trained and qualified to practice in one or more of the following specialties of dentistry; endodontics, oral and maxillofacial surgery, orthodontics and dentofacial orthopedics, pedodontics, periodontics and prosthodontics.
17-92.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-94.title: DENTIST
17-94.description: An individual who practices general dentistry or who is a manager, proprietor, operator or conductor of a place where dental services are performed for compensation. Dental services include diagnosis, treatment, prescribing or operating by X-rays, extracting teeth, correcting for malposition of teeth or jaw, administering local or general anesthetics, taking impressions of teeth and jaw, filling, crowning, bridges, plates or dentures relative to diseases, pain, deforming, deficiency, injury or physical conditions of human teeth, alveolar process, gums or jaw.
17-94.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-191.title: LICENSED DIETITIAN NUTRITIONIST
17-191.description: A person licensed by the department to practice dietetics. Dietetics includes all aspects of nutrition care for individuals and groups, including, but not limited to, nutrition assessment, nutrition counseling, nutrition education, nutrition services, and medical nutrition care. Activities of a licensed dietitian do not include the medical differential diagnosis of the health status of an individual.
17-191.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-195.title: LICENSED DIETITIAN/NUTRITION COUNSELOR
17-195.description: A person licensed by the department to provide nutrition services. Nutrition services to individuals and groups include, but are not limited to, nutrition assessments, nutrition education, nutrition counseling and nutrition care. Activities of a licensed nutrition counselor do not include medical nutrition care and medical differential diagnosis of the health status of an individual.
17-195.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-460.title: COAL MINE ELECTRICIAN RENEWAL
17-460.description: A person who performs basic maintenance, calibration and testing of electrical equipment, lines and machinery underground in the mine. Install and commission high voltage underground transformers and switches.

17-459.title: COAL MINE ELECTRICIAN SURFACE
17-459.description: A person who performs basic maintenance, calibration and testing of electrical equipment, lines and machinery in the mine, on the surface. Install and commission high voltage surface transformers and switches.

17-112.title: ELECTRICAL HOISTING ENGINEER
17-112.description: An individual responsible for the safe operation of the electrical and mechanical components of a hoist when workers are being raised or lowered into or out of a coal mine. Responsible for the daily safety check of the hoist.
17-112.agency: Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training

17-453.title: ELEVATOR APPRENTICE OR HELPER
17-453.description: A person working toward becoming an elevator mechanic. Nearly all elevator mechanics learn through a 4-year apprenticeship, are fully trained and become mechanics.

17-454.title: ELEVATOR CONTRACTOR
17-454.description: A person who is a member of the National Association of Elevator Contractors (NAEC) is qualified in compliance with industry codes, elevator and escalator specific technical theory, components, and competencies.

17-451.title: ELEVATOR INSPECTOR
17-451.description: A person who performs safety inspections of elevators, escalators, moving walkways, and other lifts. Elevator mechanics certified as Qualified Elevator Inspectors through the National Association of Elevator Safety Authorities.

17-452.title: ELEVATOR MECHANIC
17-452.description: A person who fixes, and maintains elevators, escalators, moving walkways, and other lifts. Certified Elevator Technician (CET) certification provides the industry means of gaining and verifying knowledge.

17-23.title: TEMPORARY ELEVATOR MECHANIC
17-23.description: A person hired on a short-term basis who is skilled to perform maintenance, repairs, or installations of conveyances (elevators).

17-147.title: FUNERAL DIRECTOR AND EMBALMER
17-147.description: An individual who makes funeral arrangements; prepares, directs or supervises the burial or disposal of deceased human bodies; or performs any act or service in connection with the preparation of the deceased human body. The operation of a place for the preparation for the disposition of deceased human bodies or for caring for deceased human bodies prior to their disposition is also the practice of funeral directing and embalming as is the assumption of custody and the transportation and disposition of deceased human remains.
17-147.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-550.title: A - EMT - ADVANCED EMERGENCY MEDICAL TECHNICIAN
17-550.description: An ndividual who possesses the basic knowledge and skills necessary to provide patient care and transportation. Advanced Emergency Medical Technicians function as part of a comprehensive EMS response, under medical oversight.

17-551.title: EMR - EMERGENCY MEDICAL RESPONDER
17-551.description: A person who provides first response services prior to arrival of an ambulance or specialized emergency medical services vehicle.

17-118.title: EMT - EMERGENCY MEDICAL TECHNICIAN
17-118.description: An individual licensed to function in an ambulance and provide basic life support, intermediate life support or advanced life support services under the direction of an EMS medical director at an approved resource hospital.

17-117.title: EMT- I - EMERGENCY MEDICAL TECHNICIAN - INTERMEDIATE
17-117.description: An individual licensed to function in an ambulance and provide intermediate life support services under the direction of an EMS medical director at an approved resource hospital.

17-140.title: PEMR - PROVISIONAL EMERGENCY MEDICAL RESPONDER
17-140.description: A person who provides first response services prior to arrival of an ambulance or specialized emergency medical services vehicle.

17-126.title: ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH PRACTITIONER
17-126.description: A person who, by virtue of education and experience in the physical, chemical, biological, and environmental health sciences, is especially trained to organize, implement, and manage environmental health programs; is trained to carry out education and enforcement activities for the promotion and protection of public health and the environment; and is licensed as an environmental health practitioner.
17-126.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-169.title: RADON MEASUREMENT PROFESSIONAL
17-169.description: Persons or individuals who perform services to detect or reduce the presence of radon or radon progeny.

17-301.title: RADON MEASUREMENT TECHNICIAN
17-301.description: Persons or individuals who perform services to detect or reduce the presence of radon or radon progeny.

17-302.title: RADON MITIGATION PROFESSIONAL
17-302.description: Persons or individuals who perform services to detect or reduce the presence of radon or radon progeny.

17-303.title: RADON MITIGATION TECHNICIAN
17-303.description: Persons or individuals who perform services to detect or reduce the presence of radon or radon progeny.

17-127.title: ESTHETICIAN
17-127.description: An individual who engages in beautifying, massaging, cleansing, exfoliating the stratum corneum of the epidermis, or stimulating the skin of the human body, except the scalp, by the use of cosmetic preparations, body treatments, body wraps, hydrotherapy, antiseptics, tonics, lotions or creams, or any device, electrical or otherwise for the care of the skin. Applies makeup or eyelashes to any person. Tints eyelashes and eyebrows and lightens hair on the body, except the scalp. Removes superfluous hair from the body by the use of depilatories, waxing or tweezers.
17-127.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-9.title: AQUACULTURIST
17-9.description: An individual engaged in the breeding, hatching, propagation, or raising of aquatic life, whether indigenous or non-indigenous to Illinois.

17-154.title: GINSENG DEALERS, RESIDENT AND NON-RESIDENT
17-154.description: Any person engaged in the business of buying wild or cultivated ginseng from homesteads, growers or other dealers for resale.

17-155.title: GINSENG GROWER
17-155.description: Any person engaged in the propagation and harvesting of cultivated ginseng.

17-289.title: PRESERVE AREA OPERATOR, GAMING, BREEDING, AND SHOOTING
17-289.description: Any person who establishes and maintains a game breeding and hunting preserve area for propagating, preserving and hunting game birds.

17-476.title: TA FEDERAL PLANTS
17-476.description: A person who sells plants must be licensed. The nursery program inspection staff of the Illinois Department of Agriculture's Bureau of Environmental Programs inspects and certifies nearly 900 nurseries in Illinois each year.

17-177.title: INVESTMENT ADVISOR REPRESENTATIVE
17-177.description: An individual who, for compensation, engages in the business of advising others, either directly or through publications or writings, as to the value of securities or the advisability of investing in, purchasing, or selling securities or who, for direct or indirect compensation and as part of a regular advisory business, issues or promulgates analysis or reports concerning securities.
17-177.agency: Illinois Secretary of State Securities Department

00-FinOpL.title: Series 39 - Direct Participation Programs Limited Principal
00-FinOpL.description: Covered supervisory activities and products include regulatory compliance over sales of: ?Direct participation program limited partnerships (e.g., real estate, oil and gas, and equipment leasing) ?Limited liability companies ?S corporations In addition to sales supervision, the Series 39 qualifies a principal for the overall supervision of a firm’s investment banking and securities business—including compliance, underwriting and advertising—for those activities specially covered by each supervisory principal’s license.

17-8.title: BASIC OPERATIONS FIREFIGHTER
17-8.description: An entry-level firefighter who is trained to respond to emergencies and provide services to the public.

17-185.title: LANDFILL PRIOR CONDUCT CERTIFICATION
17-185.description: An individual responsible for the management and operation of a waste disposal site on a 24-hour basis.

17-242.title: NUISANCE WILDLIFE CONTROL OPERATOR
17-242.description: Any individual who removes and/or excludes nuisance wildlife from residences. Controls crop and livestock depredation.

17-96.title: DETECTION OF DECEPTION EXAMINER
17-96.description: An individual who, by use of a device or instrument, tests or questions a person for the purpose of evaluating truthfulness or untruthfulness.
17-96.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-97.title: DETECTION OF DECEPTION TRAINEE
17-97.description: An individual who agrees to study under the direct supervision of approved instructors for the purpose of meeting requirements necessary to sit for an examination that will lead to licensure as a detection examiner.
17-97.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-GenCoun.title: Genetic Counselor
17-GenCoun.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-478.title: GENETIC COUNSELORS
17-478.description: A person who assess individual or family risk for a variety of inherited conditions, such as genetic disorders and birth defects.
17-478.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-196.title: LICENSED PROFESSIONAL GEOLOGIST
17-196.description: A person who provides the following services: mapping, sampling, and analysis of earth materials, interpretation of data, and the preparation of oral or written testimony regarding the probable geological causes of events; planning, review and supervision of data-gathering activities, interpretation of geological data gathered by direct or indirect means, preparation of geological maps, cross-sections, interpretive maps and reports for the purpose of evaluating regional or site-specific geological conditions; the planning, review, and supervision of data-gathering activities and interpretation of data on regional or site-specific geological characteristics affecting groundwater; the interpretation of geological conditions on the surface and at the depth of a specific site on Earth's surface for the purpose of determining whether those conditions correspond to a geologic map of the site; and the conducting of environmental property audits.
17-196.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-13.title: ASBESTOS AIR SAMPLING PROFESSIONAL
17-13.description: An individual who conducts or supervises all air sampling pursuant to the Commercial and Public Building Asbestos Abatement Act and the Illinois Asbestos Abatement Act for schools (Kindergarten through 12th grade) in Illinois.
17-13.agency: Illinois Department of Public Health Division of Environmental Health · Illinois Department of Public Health Division of Environmental Health

17-14.title: ASBESTOS CONTRACTOR
17-14.description: Any entity that provides removal, enclosure, encapsulation, or disposal of asbestos-containing materials pursuant to the Illinois Asbestos Abatement Act, the Illinois Commercial and Public Building Act and Code.
17-14.agency: Illinois Department of Public Health Division of Environmental Health · Illinois Department of Public Health Division of Environmental Health

17-189.title: LEAD INSPECTOR
17-189.description: An individual who inspects or samples dwellings for the presence of lead in paint, dust, soil, or other environmental sources and conducts abatement clearance testing.

17-413.title: LEAD RISK ASSESSOR
17-413.description: A person inspecting houses and other dwellings for lead-based paint contamination and identifying other potential sources of lead in strict adherence to established policies and procedures.

17-414.title: LEAD SUPERVISOR
17-414.description: A person responsible for training, quality control, and customer communication. Leads a team of front-line employees. Willingness to lead, take charge, and offer opinions and direction required.

17-415.title: LEAD WORKER
17-415.description: A person who provides leadership and instruction so others in the group can complete tasks quickly and effectively. They serve as guides to answer questions, offer insight and organize responsibilities.

17-120.title: LI - EMS LEAD INSTRUCTOR
17-120.description: A person currently approved by the department to coordinate or teach education, training and continuing education courses.

17-245.title: NURSING HOME ADMINISTRATOR
17-245.description: A licensed individual who is directly responsible for planning, organizing, directing, and supervising the operation of a nursing home, or who in fact performs such functions, whether or not such functions are delegated to one or more other persons.
17-245.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-246.title: NURSING HOME ADMINISTRATOR TEMPORARY CERTIFICATE
17-246.description: A licensed individual who is directly responsible for planning, organizing, directing, and supervising the operation of a nursing home, or who in fact performs such functions, whether or not such functions are delegated to one or more other persons.
17-246.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-348.title: LICENSED CLINICAL SOCIAL WORKER
17-348.description: A person who provides mental health services for the evaluation, treatment, and prevention of mental and emotional disorders in individuals, families and groups based on knowledge and theory of psychosocial development, behavior psychopathology, unconscious motivation, interpersonal relationships, and environmental stress. Treatment includes individual, marital, family and group psychotherapy.
17-348.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-347.title: LICENSED SOCIAL WORKER
17-347.description: A person who is engaged in social services to individuals, social group work, community organizations for social welfare, social work research, social welfare administration or social work education.
17-347.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-217.title: HEARING INSTRUMENT DISPENSER
17-217.description: Any person who sells to and services hearing instruments for the deaf/hard of hearing.
17-217.agency: Illinois Department of Public Health · Division of Health Assessment and Screening

17-83.title: COUNSELOR, PRIVATE EMPLOYMENT AGENCY
17-83.description: An individual who furnishes information to an individual as to where employees or employment may be obtained or found.

00-Ins.title: NIPR Insurance Registry
00-Ins.description: Licensed Insurance Occupations must also be registered at the federal level.

17-44.title: BROKER, MEAT/POULTRY/MEAT AND POULTRY
17-44.description: Any person engaged in buying and re-selling meat and poultry products without altering the products in any matter.

17-111.title: EGG PRODUCER-DEALER/PRODUCER-PACKER/GRADER/DISTRIBUTOR/JOBBER-BROKER
17-111.description: A person who feeds and houses poultry and obtains their eggs. Grades, sizes, candles, or packs eggs for sale to consumers, manufactures or retailers. Distributes eggs or egg products.

17-12.title: LIMITED ELEVATOR CONTRACTOR
17-12.description: A person or company who is licensed by the state to carry on a business of erecting, constructing, installing, altering, servicing, repairing, or maintaining a specific type of conveyance (elevators) within any building or structure, excluding private residences.

17-22.title: LIMITED ELEVATOR MECHANIC
17-22.description: A person who constructs, modernizes, repairs or services conveyances (elevators).

17-200.title: LIVESTOCK BUYER/BROKER/SLAUGHTER
17-200.description: A Buyer is an individual who purchases livestock for the purpose of slaughtering it for food and selling the meat products there from. A Broker is an individual who buys slaughtered livestock from the producer for resale to a meat plant.

17-329.title: SEED BROKER
17-329.description: An individual who sells seed belonging to others for resale on a commission basis.

17-410.title: VIATICAL SETTLEMENT BROKER
17-410.description: Someone who negotiates a viatical settlement on behalf of a life insurance policy owner.

17-170.title: INTERIOR DESIGNER
17-170.description: A person, qualified by education, experience, and examinations, who administers contracts for fabrication, procurement, or installation in the implementation of designs, drawings, and specifications for any interior design project. Offers or furnishes professional services, such as consultations, studies drawings, and specifications in connection with location of lighting fixtures, lamps, and specifications of ceiling finishes as shown in reflected ceiling plans, space planning, furnishings, or the fabrication of non-loadbearing structural elements within and surrounding interior spaces of buildings, but specifically excluding mechanical and electrical systems, except for specifications of fixtures and their location within interior spaces.
17-170.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-43.title: PROFESSIONAL EDUCATOR LICENSE
17-43.description: A certified individual to work as a teacher or educator in a specific subject or grade level.
17-43.agency: Dept. of Teacher Educ. and Certification · Illinois State Board of Education

17-50.title: TEACHER, EARLY CHILDHOOD
17-50.description: A person works directly with children in an eligible preschool program or eligible early childhood education program in a low-income community.
17-50.agency: Dept. of Teacher Educ. and Certification · Illinois State Board of Education

17-186.title: LANDSCAPE ARCHITECT
17-186.description: An individual who is engaged in the art and science of arranging land, together with the spaces and objects upon it, for creating a safe, efficient, healthful, and aesthetically pleasing physical environment for human use and enjoyment.
17-186.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-188.title: LAWYER (ATTORNEY-AT-LAW - NEWLY REGISTERED)
17-188.description: An individual who counsels people on legal courses of action in business or personal matters. A lawyer may represent one of the opposing parties in criminal and civil trials by presenting arguments that support the client in a court of law.

17-148.title: FUNERAL DIRECTOR AND EMBALMER INTERN
17-148.description: A person who is qualified to render assistance to a licensed funeral director and embalmer in carrying out the practice of funeral directing and embalming. All assistance must be performed under the direct supervision of a licensed funeral director and embalmer.
17-148.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-176.title: INVESTMENT ADVISER
17-176.description: An individual who, for compensation, engages in the business of advising others, either directly or through publications or writings, as to the value of securities or the advisability of investing in, purchasing, or selling securities or who, for direct or indirect compensation and as part of a regular advisory business, issues or promulgates analysis or reports concerning securities.
17-176.agency: Illinois Secretary of State Securities Department

17-475.title: TYPE II STATE PLANTS (CUSTOM INSPECTION)
17-475.description: A person who works in a capacity to receive live animals and or poultry for slaughter and processing as a service only for owner's personal household use. Not produced under inspection and not elibible for sale in commerce.

17-202.title: LOAN BROKERS
17-202.description: Persons who, in return for a fee from any person who is domiciled in the State of Illinois, promise to procure a loan for any person or assist any person in procuring a loan from any third party, or who promise to consider whether or not to make a loan to any person. Must be registered as a loan broker with the Secretary of State, unless exempt under law.
17-202.agency: Illinois Secretary of State Securities Department

17-255.title: OWNER OF CREDIT SERVICES ORGANIZATION (BUSINESS)
17-255.description: An individual who, with respect to the extension of credit by others and in return for the payment of money or other valuable consideration, provides or represents that the person can or will provide any of the following services: (i) improving a buyer's credit record, history, or rating; (ii) obtaining an extension of credit for a buyer; or (iii) providing assistance to a buyer with regard to either (i) or (ii).
17-255.agency: Illinois Secretary of State Index Department

17-204.title: LOCKSMITH
17-204.description: An individual who engages in the practice of locksmithing. That includes, but is not limited to, the servicing, installing, originating first keys, re-coding, repairing, maintaining, manipulating, or bypassing of mechanical or electronic locking device, access control, or video surveillance system at premises, vehicles, safes, vaults, safe deposit boxes, or automatic teller machines.
17-204.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-243.title: NURSE, LICENSED PRACTICAL
17-243.description: An individual who assists in the care of the ill, injured, and disabled persons. Under the supervision of registered nurses, physicians, dentists or podiatrists, the licensed practical nurse administers certain medications, monitors equipment, cleans dressings, take temperatures and blood pressures, and assists patients with personal hygiene.
17-243.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-193.title: LICENSED NAIL TECHNICIAN
17-193.description: A person who provides the following services: manicures, pedicures, decorates nails, applies sculptured or other artificial nails, or in any way cares for the nails or skin of the hands or feet including massaging the hands, arms, elbows, feet, lower legs and knees for other than the treatment of medical disorders.
17-193.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-294.title: LICENSED PROFESSIONAL COUNSELOR
17-294.description: A person who provides services to individuals, couples, groups, families, and organizations in any one or more of the fields of professional counseling.
17-294.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-164.title: MARRIAGE AND FAMILY THERAPIST
17-164.description: An individual who provides marriage and family therapy services to individuals, couples and families and evaluates and treats mental and emotional problems within the context of human relationships.
17-164.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-479.title: MASSAGE THERAPISTS
17-479.description: A person who perform therapeutic massages of soft tissues and joints. May assist in the assessment of range of motion and muscle strength, or propose client therapy plans.
17-479.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-MassTher.title: Massage Therapy
17-MassTher.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

00-52.title: Assistant Engineer (Limited - Oceans)
00-52.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as an Assistant Engineer (Limited - Oceans) include 1,080 days at sea, with 540 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-52.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-47.title: First Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-47.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a First Assistant Engineer - Upper Level, the applicant must complete 360 days of service as a Second or Third Assistant Engineer; while holding a Second Assistant Engineer license. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations
00-47.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-49.title: Third Assistant Engineer - Upper Level
00-49.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Third Assistant Engineer (upper Level, the applicant must complete one of the following: 1080 days of service in the engine room with 720 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED); or 1080 days as a machinist apprentice engaged in construction or repair of marine, locomotive, or stationary engines plus 360 days of sea service in an engine room as oiler, watertender, or jr. engineer; or graduate from an approved course of studies. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-49.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

17-181.title: LABORATORY ANALYSIS OF RADON DEVICES
17-181.description: Individuals who perform services to detect or reduce the presence of radon or radon progeny.

17-241.title: NUCLEAR MEDICINE TECHNOLOGIST
17-241.description: A person, other than a licensed practitioner, who administers radio pharmaceuticals and related drugs to human beings for diagnostic purposes. Performs in vivo and in vitro detection and measurement of radioactivity. Administers radio pharmaceuticals to human beings for therapeutic purposes. A nuclear medicine technologist may perform such procedures only while under the supervision of a licensed practitioner who is licensed to possess and use radioactive materials.

00-10.title: Nuclear Facility Operator
00-10.description: Nuclear Facility Operators are required to have either training or experience to become licensed. They must pass a medical exam, a written test, and an operating test. Although the license is granted for 6 years, licensees must pass another medical exam every two years and an operating test annually. Also, they must undergo requalification training while employed. Nuclear Facility Senior Operators have additional experience and pass another exam to be promoted from Nuclear Facility Operators. Further information can be found at the web site: http://www.nrc.gov/reactors/operator-licensing.html

00-63.title: Hospital Corpsman
00-63.description: A Hospital Corpsman is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A hospital corpsman must have U.S. military experience as and a rating of hospital corpsman or Health Services Technician or equivalent.
