Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-63.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

17-209.title: MINE EXAMINER
17-209.description: An individual responsible for the varied inspections and examinations that are required by the Coal Mining Act, i.e. ventilation, rock dusting, and dangerous or potentially dangerous work areas, escapements, shafts and seals. Works directly for the mine manager.
17-209.agency: Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training · Illinois Department of Natural Resources Office of Mines and Minerals, Division of Mine Safety and Training

17-247.title: OCCUPATIONAL THERAPIST
17-247.description: An individual engaged in the evaluation, after physician referral for occupational therapy as part of the total rehabilitation and health care team, of functional performance ability of person impaired by physical illness or injury, emotional disorder, congenital or developmental disability or the aging process and the analysis, selection and application of occupations or goal directed activities, for the treatment or prevention of the disabilities to achieve optimum functioning.
17-247.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-350.title: CERTIFIED LANDFILL OPERATOR
17-350.description: An individual who is on the operational staff of a landfill, involved in the operation and maintenance of a non-hazardous sanitary landfill.

17-464.title: TEMPORARY MINE MANAGER
17-464.description: A person who is responsible for scheduling staff and ensuring that supplies are stocked. They play a direct role in developing business goals for the mine, help to produce a business plan to ensure that those goals are met.

17-206.title: MAIL-ORDER OPHTHALMIC PROVIDER
17-206.description: Any non-resident entity that dispenses contact lenses through the United States Postal Service or other common carrier to Illinois residents.
17-206.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-251.title: LICENSED OPTOMETRIST
17-251.description: An individual who engages in the examination of the human eye and its appendages without the use of medicine or surgery. Includes the appropriate use of topical ocular pharmaceutical agents for examination and diagnostic purposes, for ascertaining any departure from the normal, measuring powers of vision, and adapting lenses of prisms, diagnosis, prescription, and management of contact lenses, ocular exercises, and visual therapy.
17-251.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-252.title: LICENSED ORTHOTICS, PROSTHETICS, AND PEDORTHICS
17-252.description: Orthodist: An individual who measures, designs, fabricates, fits, or services orthoses and assists in the formulation of the order or orthoses as ordered by a licensed physician for the support or correction of disabilities caused by neuro-musculoskeletal disease, injuries, or deformities. Pedorthist: An individual who measures, designs, fabricates, fits, or services prostheses and assists in the formulation of the order or prostheses as ordered by a licensed physician for the support or correction of disabilities caused by neuro-musculoskeletal disease, injuries, or deformities. Prosthetist: An individual who measures, designs, fabricates, fits or services prostheses and assists in the formulation of the order of prostheses as ordered by a licensed physician for the replacement of external parts of the human body lost due to amputation or congenital deformities or absences.
17-252.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-248.title: OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY ASSISTANT
17-248.description: An individual who assists a registered occupational therapist and, under their supervision, implements the occupational therapy treatment program. Such a program may include training in activities of daily living, use of therapeutic activity, and guidance in the selection and use of adaptive equipment.
17-248.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-552.title: PARAMEDIC
17-552.description: A person who provides treatment, such as first aid or life support care, to sick or injured patients. Prepare patients for and safely transport them to the emergency department of a hospital or other healthcare facility.

17-264.title: PEST CONTROL TECHNICIAN (RESTRICTED USE), STRUCTURAL
17-264.description: An individual who performs pest control services including the use of restricted pesticides in and around structures (as opposed to applications of pesticides in agriculture).

17-273.title: PHARMACIST, REGISTERED
17-273.description: Any person who compounds, dispenses, sells or offers for sale, makes recommendations or advises persons concerning the contents and/or the therapeutic uses of medicines, poisons pursuant to prescription or orders from a person authorized to prescribe such drugs.
17-273.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-274.title: PHARMACY TECHNICIAN
17-274.description: An individual authorized to assist in the practice of pharmacy under the personal supervision of a registered pharmacist.
17-274.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-275.title: PHYSICAL THERAPIST
17-275.description: An individual who is involved in the evaluation or treatment of a person by the use of effective properties of physical measures and heat, cold, light, water, radiant energy, electricity, sound, and air. Uses therapeutic massage, therapeutic exercise, mobilization, and rehabilitative procedures for the purpose of preventing, correcting, or alleviating a physical or mental disability or promoting physical fitness and well-being.
17-275.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-276.title: PHYSICAL THERAPIST ASSISTANT
17-276.description: An individual licensed to assist and work under the supervision of a physical therapist in implementing patients' physical therapy treatment programs as established by the licensed physical therapist. Patient care activities provided by the physical therapy assistant do not include interpretation of referrals, evaluation procedures, planning of or major modifications of patient programs.
17-276.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

00-80.title: Marine Physician Assistant
00-80.description: A Marine Physician Assistant is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A physician assistant must also have training as a physician's assistant or nurse practitioner. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-80.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

17-280.title: PHYSICIAN ASSISTANT
17-280.description: An individual who is not a physician nor a person holding an M.D. or equivalent degree who has been certified as a physician assistant by the National Commission on Certification of Physician Assistants or equivalent successor agency and performs procedures under the supervision of a physician as defined in the Physician's Assistant Practice Act.
17-280.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

00-31.title: Tankerman
00-31.description: Tankerman refers to several endorsements or qualified ratings to Merchant Marine Documents (MMD). All Tankerman endorsements require qualifying experience, training in firefighting and cargo (dangerous liquids or liquefied gasses), and passing an exam. Endorsements include Tankerman - Person-In-Charge (Tankerman PIC), Tankerman-Engineer, Tankerman Assistant, and Tankerman - PIC (Barge). Tankerman endorsements are valid for the duration of the MMD, which is issued for 5 years. Renewal of certification requires meeting all the requirements to renew the MMD and either have recent qualifying experience or training. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR13.109) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr13_02.html.
00-31.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

17-467.title: FIRE SPRINKLERS CONTRACTORS
17-467.description: A person who is liscensed to provide services related to fire sprinklers to general contractors, management companies and private homeowners.

17-284.title: PLUMBER
17-284.description: An individual who installs water supply and distribution lines and drain, waste and vent systems within and throughout houses and other buildings.

17-285.title: PLUMBER, APPRENTICE
17-285.description: An individual who installs water supply and distribution lines and drain, waste and vent systems throughout houses and other buildings under the supervision of a licensed plumber.

17-335.title: SEWAGE DISPOSAL SYSTEM PUMPING CONTRACTOR, PRIVATE
17-335.description: An individual who pumps septage from private sewage disposal systems.

17-403.title: WATER WELL AND PUMP INSTALLATION CONTRACTOR
17-403.description: An individual who drills and constructs water wells and installs water well pumps.

17-404.title: WATER WELL CONTRACTOR
17-404.description: An individual who drills or does construction on water wells.

17-405.title: WATER WELL PUMP INSTALLATION CONTRACTOR
17-405.description: An individual who installs and repairs water well pumps.

17-287.title: LICENSED PODIATRIC PHYSICIAN
17-287.description: An individual who practices podiatric medicine which involves the diagnosis, medical, physical or surgical treatment of the ailments of the human foot with the exception of administrations of general anesthetics and the amputation of the foot.
17-287.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-286.title: TEMPORARY PODIATRIC PHYSICIAN
17-286.description: A podiatric physician otherwise qualified for licensure with the exception of completion of one year postgraduate residency program approved by the CPME and the exception of successful completion of the Written Clinical Competency Examination required under Section 10 of the Podiatric Medical Practice Act.
17-286.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-291.title: LICENSED PRIVATE DETECTIVE
17-291.description: An individual who engages in a business or accepts employment to furnish, or agrees to make or makes investigations with reference to such acts as: 1) crimes or wrongs done or threats against the United States or any state or U.S. territory; 2) the location, disposition or recovery of lost or stolen property; 3) securing evidence to be used before any court, board, officer or investigating committee; 4) personal protection of individuals from bodily harm or death.
17-291.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-6.title: PRODUCTION COMPANY DISTRUBUTOR
17-6.description: A person responsible for the marketing of a film.

17-7.title: PRODUCTION COMPANY OPERATOR
17-7.description: A person tasked with setting up, monitoring, and maintaining machines and equipment used in production lines

00-05.title: Customs Broker
00-05.description: Customs brokers must pass an exam to obtain a license. Further information can be found at the US Customs Service web site: http://www.customs.gov/xp/cgov/import/broker_management/.

00-59.title: Purser
00-59.description: The Purser, one of a ship's staff officers, is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A Junior Assistant Purser requires no experience. A Senior Assistant Purser requires 180 days, a Purser requires 360 days, and a Chief Purser requires 720 days of service aboard vessels while performing duties related to the purser's office. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-59.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

17-486.title: REAL ESTATE BROKER
17-486.description: A Real Estate Broker, or Managing Real Estate Broker, is responsible for overseeing real estate transactions between buyers and sellers.
17-486.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-296.title: CLINICAL PSYCHOLOGIST
17-296.description: An individual who provides the independent evaluation, classification and treatment of mental, emotional, behavioral or nervous disorders or conditions, disorders of habit or conduct, and the psychological aspects of physical illness. The practice of clinical psychology includes psychoeducational evaluation, therapy, remediation and consultation, the use of psychological and neuropsychological testing, assessment, psychotherapy, psychoanalysis, hypnosis, biofeedback, and behavioral modification when any of these are used for the purpose of preventing or eliminating psychopathology, or for the amelioration of psychological disorders of individuals or groups.
17-296.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-165.title: RADIATION THERAPIST
17-165.description: A person, other than a licensed practitioner, who performs procedures and applies ionizing radiation emitted from X-ray machines, particle accelerators, or sealed radioactive sources to human beings for therapeutic purposes while under the supervision of a licensed practitioner.

17-166.title: RADIOGRAPHER, INDUSTRIAL
17-166.description: An individual who uses radioactive materials, or radiation producing machines to perform examination of macroscopic structures in fabricated materials or processes.

17-167.title: RADIOGRAPHER, MEDICAL
17-167.description: A person, other than a licensed practitioner, who, while under the supervision of a licensed practitioner, applies X-radiation to any part of the human body and who, in conjunction with radiation studies, may administer contrast agents and related drugs for diagnostic purposes.

17-168.title: RADIOGRAPHER, MEDICAL (LIMITED)
17-168.description: A person, other than a licensed practitioner, who, while under the supervision of a licensed practitioner, applies X-radiation to limited parts of the human body for diagnostic purposes. The categories of limited accreditation are: chest, extremities, spine, and skull and sinuses.

17-366.title: THERAPEUTIC RADIOLOGICAL PHYSICIST
17-366.description: A person who possesses the knowledge, training and experience to apply the principles of radiological physics to therapeutic X-ray applications. This involves implementation and maintenance of a comprehensive radiation protection program, to include annual performance evaluations of therapeutic X-ray equipment and assurance that such equipment is being maintained and operated in accordance with standards established by the agency.

17-REBranch.title: Real Estate Branch Office
17-REBranch.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-485.title: REAL ESTATE BRANCH OFFICE
17-485.description: A principal broker's real estate brokerage office other than the principal broker's main office
17-485.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-480.title: REAL ESTATE BROKER CORPORATION
17-480.description: A person who operate real estate office, or work for commercial real estate firm, overseeing real estate transactions. Other duties usually include selling real estate or renting properties and arranging loans.
17-480.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-488.title: REAL ESTATE BROKER CORPORATION
17-488.description: A corporate real estate is the real property held or used by a business enterprise or organization for its own operational purposes. A corporate real estate portfolio typically includes a corporate headquarters and a number of branch offices, and perhaps also various manufacturing and retail sites.
17-488.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-482.title: REAL ESTATE BROKER PARTNERSHIP
17-482.description: A real estate partnership is formed by two or more investors who combine their capital and expertise to purchase, develop, or lease property.
17-482.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-487.title: REAL ESTATE CE INSTRUCTOR
17-487.description: A real estate instructor offers pre-licensing training to individuals preparing to take state exams for real estate agents.
17-487.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-REInCE.title: Real Estate CE Instructor - In Renewal
17-REInCE.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-RECE.title: Real Estate CE School
17-RECE.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-RECorp.title: Real Estate Corporation
17-RECorp.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-490.title: REAL ESTATE EDUCATION PROVIDER
17-490.description: An institution that helps enhancing knowledge of market trends and regulations to improving communication and negotiation skills, continued education leads to a strong foundation and competitive edge.
17-490.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-RELeas.title: Real Estate Leasing Agent
17-RELeas.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-REAgent.title: Real Estate Leasing Agent Student
17-REAgent.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-484.title: REAL ESTATE LEASING AGENT STUDENT
17-484.description: A person who attends Pre licensing course related to leasing residential property for students seeking agent licensure.
17-484.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-RELLC.title: Real Estate LLC
17-RELLC.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-REPart.title: Real Estate Partnership
17-REPart.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-489.title: REAL ESTATE PRE-LICENSE INSTRUCTOR
17-489.description: A Pre-License Instructor License will qualify you to teach all Pre-License Courses for Salespersons and Brokers unless the license is "restricted" by the Office of Banks and Real Estate.
17-489.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-492.title: REAL ESTATE PRE-LICENSE INSTRUCTOR
17-492.description: An individual possessing a Real Estate Pre-License Instructor License may teach any Pre-License, Post-License, and Continuing Education (“CE”) Course licensed by the Division of Real Estate (“DRE”), unless restricted by the DRE to specific courses or topic areas.
17-492.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-REIn.title: Real Estate Pre-License Instructor - In Renewal
17-REIn.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-RELicSch.title: Real Estate Pre-License School
17-RELicSch.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-RESchool.title: Real Estate Pre-License School Branch
17-RESchool.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-483.title: REAL ESTATE RESIDENTIAL LEASING AGENT
17-483.description: A person who work with property owners to market and show their residential properties and attract good tenants and they also help renters find and lease properties.
17-483.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-REBrok.title: Real Estate Broker
17-REBrok.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-REMan.title: Real Estate Managing Broker
17-REMan.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-481.title: REAL ESTATE MANAGING BROKER
17-481.description: A person who is responsible for overseeing real estate transactions between buyers and sellers.
17-481.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-323.title: SCRAP PROCESSOR
17-323.description: Any person in the business that purchases a vehicle, junk vehicle or vehicle cowl for processing into a form other than a vehicle, junk vehicle or vehicle cowl for remelting purposes only. Utilizes machinery and equipment for processing or manufacturing ferrous or nonferrous metallic scrap into prepared grades.

17-375.title: TRANSPORTER
17-375.description: Any person in the business of transporting motor vehicles, not his/her own, by driving either singly or by the towbar, saddle mount or full mount method or any combination thereof and using the public highways of this state.
17-375.agency: Illinois Secretary of State Dealer Licensing

17-99.title: DIAGNOSTIC IMAGING SPECIALIST
17-99.description: A person who possesses the knowledge, training and experience to apply the principles of radiological physics to diagnostic X-ray applications. This involves implementation and maintenance of a comprehensive radiation protection program, to include annual performance evaluations of X-ray equipment and assurance that such equipment is being maintained and operated in accordance with standards established by the agency.

17-58.title: LICENSED RESPIRATORY CARE PRACTIONAER
17-58.description: A person who provides specialized care for lung and heart disorders.
17-58.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-RespCare.title: Respiratory Care Practitioner
17-RespCare.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-239.title: NEW VEHICLE DEALER (CLASS A - NON-COMMERCIAL, CLASS B - COMMERCIAL)
17-239.description: An individual who is in the business of selling or dealing in, on consignment or otherwise, new vehicles of any make or who acts as an intermediary, agent or broker for any licensed vehicle dealer or vehicle purchaser.
17-239.agency: Illinois Secretary of State Dealer Licensing

17-379.title: USED VEHICLE DEALER
17-379.description: Any person in the business of selling or dealing in, on consignment or otherwise, used vehicles of any make or acting as an intermediary or agent or broker for any licensed vehicle dealer or vehicle purchaser.
17-379.agency: Illinois Secretary of State Dealer Licensing

00-61.title: Professional Nurse
00-61.description: A ship's Professional Nurse is a staff officer and is required to obtain a Certificate of Registry (COR). To obtain a COR requires completing first aid and cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) training within the past 12 months and meeting medical fitness standards. A professional nurse must also hold a valid license as a registered nurse issued within the United States. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SUBPART=H&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-61.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

17-114.title: ECRN - EMERGENCY COMMUNICATION REGISTERED NURSE
17-114.description: A registered professional nurse who is approved by an Emergency Medical Services (EMS) medical director to monitor telecommunications from and give voice orders to EMS system personnel in accordance with system protocols.

17-244.title: NURSE, ADVANCED PRACTICE REGISTERED
17-244.description: An individual involved in providing health care to injured, sick, and well persons. Tasks and duties may include nursing evaluations, observation, care and counsel of the ill, impaired, or infirm; maintenance of health or prevention of illness, administration of medication and treatments as prescribed by a licensed physician or dentist; and supervision or teaching of nursing.
17-244.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-553.title: PHAPRN - PRE HOSPITAL ADVANCED PRACTICAL REGISTERED NURSE
17-553.description: A person who who receive additional education to practice in EMS systems as emergency medical services personnel.

17-412.title: PHRN - PRE HOSPITAL REGISTERED NURSE
17-412.description: A person who function as advanced life support care provider in the prehospital environment.

17-376.title: TNS - TRAUMA NURSE SPECIALIST
17-376.description: A registered professional nurse who has successfully completed education and testing requirements prescribed by the department.

17-319.title: LICENSED ROOFING CONTRACTOR
17-319.description: An individual whose services are unlimited in the roofing trade and who has experience, knowledge and skill to construct, reconstruct, alter, maintain and repair roofs in a manner that complies with all plans, specifications, and applicable codes, laws and regulations.
17-319.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

00-03.title: Able Seaman - AB
00-03.description: Requirements for an Able Seaman license include a medical certificate of excellent health, and a certificate attesting to vision, color perception, and general physical condition. While no experience or formal schooling is required, training at a union-operated school is the best source. With experience at sea, and perhaps union-sponsored training, an ordinary seaman with a Merchant Marine Document (MMD) can pass the Able Seaman exam and move up with 3 years of service. Please see the U.S. Coast Guard web site at: http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, the Veteran's Employment and Training Service (VETS) web site at http://umet-vets.dol.gov/ableseaman.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.02-11) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html
00-03.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-30.title: Lifeboatman - LBMAN
00-30.description: A person with a Merchant Marine Document (MMD) with one year of experience at sea in the deck department, two years experience in any other department on vessels greater than 100 gross tons, or who has completed a USCG approved course and 3 months of sea experience may take written and practical exams to be endorsed with the qualified rating of Lifeboatman (LB). An MMD with a qualified rating is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through documented recent experience, pass an exam, or complete a training course. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR12.10-7) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-30.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-33.title: Merchant Mariner's Document - MMD
00-33.description: The United States Coast Guard issues a Merchant Mariner's Document (MMD) to unlicensed personnel who support the operation of a vessel. Unqualified ratings are issued to entry level individuals who typically have little or no sea service for the following rating types: ordinary seaman (deck department), wiper (engineering department), or food handler (steward's department). Qualified ratings are issued based on previous sea service in a particular department or specialized training. Qualified ratings for members in the deck department are issued by rating type (e.g. Able Seaman) and vessel type restrictions (e.g. sail vessels or offshore supply vessels). Qualified ratings for members in the engineering department are issued by type (e.g. Qualified Member of the Engine Department) and specific rating (e.g. oiler, fireman/watertender, junior engineer, deck engine mechanic, or engineman). Other ratings are issued for specialized training or experience, such as Lifeboatman, Tankerman, or GMDSS At-Sea Maintainer. An MMD is valid for 5 years and may be renewed. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.02-11) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-33.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-04.title: Ordinary Seaman
00-04.description: An Ordinary Seaman is a person holding a Merchant Mariner's Document (MMD) issued by the United States Coast Guard without qualified ratings. This is an entry level MMD and does not require maritime experience or a physical examination, but will require proof that the applicant has passed a chemical test for dangerous drugs. While no training is required, a union-operated school can provide useful background knowledge. An MMD is valid for 5 years and may be renewed. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.02-11) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-04.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-32.title: Qualified Member of the Engine Department - QMED
00-32.description: Qualified Member of the Engine Department - QMED A person with a Merchant Mariner's Document (MMD) having at least 6 months of underway service working as a wiper or coal passer in the engineering department may take a written exam and at least one rating exam (Fireman/Watertender, Oiler, Deck Engineer, Junior Engineer, Refrigeration Engineer, Electrician, Machinist, or Pumpman) to be endorsed as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Additional experience is required for some endorsements. Renewal of certification requires meeting all the requirements to renew the MMD and either have recent qualifying experience or training. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46 CFR12.15-11) at website http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr12_02.html.
00-32.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

17-46.title: BUSINESS BROKERS
17-46.description: Persons who, in return for a fee, commission, or other compensation from any person who is domiciled in the State of Illinois, promises to procure a business or assist in the procurement of a business, negotiates offers, buys, sells, or otherwise deals in options on businesses, or assists or directs the procurement of prospects intended to result in the purchase, sale, exchange of a business, or advertises or represents himself as a business broker must be registered as a business broker with the Secretary of State, unless exempt under law.
17-46.agency: Illinois Secretary of State Securities Department

17-214.title: MINNOW DEALER, RETAIL AND WHOLESALE
17-214.description: Any individual who, within the state of Illinois, sells or offers live minnows for sale to any other retailer or wholesaler.

17-236.title: MUSSEL DEALER, RESIDENT AND NON-RESIDENT
17-236.description: Any individual who receives, buys, offers to, or acts as an agent or a broker in the receipt or purchase of mussels.

17-330.title: SEED DEALER, RETAIL
17-330.description: An individual who buys and sells seed from wholesalers, brokers and/or seed merchants for resale to the consumer.

17-331.title: SEED DEALER, WHOLESALE
17-331.description: A person who buys seed from producers, re-labels and repackages the seed for resale to retailers.

17-387.title: VENDOR
17-387.description: A person who sells board-approved items within the race track enclosure.

17-388.title: VENDOR'S HELPER
17-388.description: A person who is an employee of a tack shop operator or vendor.

17-407.title: AQUATIC LIFE DEALER, RETAIL & WHOLESALE
17-407.description: Any person conducting a retail or wholesale fish market or buying, selling or shipping any aquatic life (except minnows) protected by Illinois Conservation Law.

17-55.title: CERTIFIED LIVESTOCK MANAGER
17-55.description: Any person certified by the Department of Agriculture to operate a livestock waste handling facility.

17-408.title: COMMERCIAL ROE DEALER/HARVESTER
17-408.description: All commercial fishermen engaged in harvesting roe bearing species

17-134.title: FEEDER SWINE DEALER
17-134.description: An individual who buys and re-sells feeder swine.

17-156.title: GRAIN DEALER
17-156.description: An individual who is engaged in buying grain from producers for resale, milling, or processing.

17-157.title: GRAIN WAREHOUSE OPERATOR (WAREHOUSEMAN)
17-157.description: Any person who owns, controls, operates, or manages any public grain warehouse in which grain is stored for compensation.

17-477.title: HALAL CERTIFICATES
17-477.description: A person who sells food labeled halal is required to have a $75 license. It certifies that all food labeled halal is kept in the halal way and is from halal sources.

17-199.title: LIVESTOCK AUCTION MARKET OPERATOR
17-199.description: An individual who accepts consignments of livestock from the public for sale, resale, or exchange on commission.

17-201.title: LIVESTOCK DEALER
17-201.description: An individual who buys or offers to sell, exchange, barter, or negotiate the sale of cattle, goats, sheep, or swine other than feeder swine.

17-332.title: SEED MERCHANT
17-332.description: An individual who is a wholesale/retail seed dealer. Buys seed from producers. Re-labels and repackages seed and sells to retail establishment and consumers.

17-371.title: TIMBER BUYER
17-371.description: An individual who is in the business of buying timber, has knowledge of timber and log market structure, has the ability to operate in a fiscally sound manner and to complete contractual arrangements in the field of buying and selling, and has skills in business and personnel management.

17-53.title: SCHOOL ADMINISTRATOR
17-53.description: A person responsible for providing instructional leadership and developing, implementing, and evaluating district and school systems and policies.
17-53.agency: Dept. of Teacher Educ. and Certification · Illinois State Board of Education

00-InvComp.description: Covered supervisory activities and products include regulatory compliance over sales of the following. ?Mutual funds ?Closed-end funds (initial offering only) ?Variable annuities ?Variable life insurance

00-FinOp.description: Covered supervisory activities include the following. ?Back office operations ?Preparation and maintenance of a member firm’s books and records ?Compliance with financial responsibility rules that apply to self-clearing broker-dealers and market makers ?Mutual funds ?Closed-end funds (initial offering only) ?Variable annuities ?Variable life insurance

00-BrokDeal.description: Covered supervisory activities include the following. ?Back office operations ?Preparation and maintenance of a member firm’s books and records ?Compliance with financial responsibility rules that apply to fully disclosed broker-dealers that do not hold customer funds and securities, and do not carry customer accounts

00-RegOpt.description: Covered supervisory activities and products include regulatory compliance over trading, market making, underwriting and advertising of: ?Equity options ?Foreign currency options ?Interest rate options ?Index options ?Options on government and mortgage-backed securities

00-MunFund.description: Municipal fund securities (e.g., 529 College Savings Plans, Local Government Investment Pools (LGIPs))

00-MunSec.description: Municipal securities, including municipal fund securities (e.g., 529 College Savings Plans, Local Government Investment Pools (LGIPs))

17-324.title: SECURITIES DEALER
17-324.description: Any person who engages either directly or indirectly as an agent, broker or principal in the business of offering, selling, buying and selling or otherwise dealing or trading in securities.
17-324.agency: Illinois Secretary of State Securities Department

17-325.title: SECURITIES SALESPERSON
17-325.description: An individual employed by a dealer or issuer to offer, purchase or sell securities. A securities salesperson must be registered with the Secretary of State before he or she may offer, purchase or sell securities on behalf of a securities dealer, issuer or controlling person.
17-325.agency: Illinois Secretary of State Securities Department

17-75.title: COMMERCIAL DRIVER TRAINING SCHOOL OWNER
17-75.description: Any person who engages in the business of giving driver training instruction for hire or for a fee, or prepares an applicant for an examination given by the Secretary of State for a driver's license or permit.
17-75.agency: Illinois Secretary of State Department of Driver Services · Commercial Driver Training Section

17-105.title: DRIVER TRAINING INSTRUCTOR
17-105.description: An individual who teaches driver training for a fee, to adults, teenagers, or applicants required to obtain a Commercial Drivers License (CDL).
17-105.agency: Illinois Secretary of State Department of Driver Services · Commercial Driver Training Section

17-500.title: DRIVER/TRAINER
17-500.description: Any person in the horse racing industry, who is able to drive and train a standard bred (harness) horse which pulls a sulky at either a trot or pace.

00-28.title: Ocean Transportation Intermediary - OTI
00-28.description: Licensure as an Ocean Transportation Intermediary (OTI) - Ocean Freight Forwarder requires that the designated employee for the company have three years of qualifying experience, meet character requirements, and be bonded. The license is issued indefinitely or until revoked or suspended. Details can be found at the FMC web sites http://www.fmc.gov/cfr/515.htm, http://www.fmc.gov/Help/OTI.htm, and the Code of Federal Regulations (46CFR515) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr515_02.html.
00-28.agency: Federal Maritime Commission · Bureau of Tariffs, Certification and Licensing

00-29.title: Ocean Transportation Intermediary -NVOCC
00-29.description: Licensure as an Ocean Transportation Intermediary (OTI)- Non-Vessel-Operating Common Carrier (NVOCC) requires that the qualifying individual for the company have three years of qualifying experience, meet character requirements, and be bonded. The license is issued indefinitely or until revoked or suspended. Details can be found at the FMC web sites: http://www.fmc.gov/cfr/515.htm, http://www.fmc.gov/Help/OTI.htm, and the Code of Federal Regulations (46CFR515) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr515_02.html.
00-29.agency: Federal Maritime Commission · Bureau of Tariffs, Certification and Licensing

17-11.title: ART AUCTION HOUSE OWNER
17-11.description: Any person, partnership, corporation, association or group engaged for profit primarily in the business of conducting auctions at which they act as agent for any seller of works of art, antiques, furnishings, jewelry, gemstones, coins, stamps, and rare books and manuscripts.
17-11.agency: Illinois Secretary of State Index Department

17-386.title: VEHICLE AUCTIONEER
17-386.description: An individual who sells, solicits, and advertises the sale of used vehicles, belonging to others, at auction.
17-386.agency: Illinois Secretary of State Dealer Licensing

00-67.title: Barge Supervisor
00-67.description: A Barge Supervisor is required to pass an exam, have 3 years of related work experience or an approved degree in engineering or engineering technology, plus at least 168 days of related experience. Specialized training is also required in stability of the mobile offshore drilling unit (ODU), survival at sea, and firefighting. Federal regulations can be found at the web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-67.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-37.title: Chief Mate - Upper Level
00-37.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Mate - Upper Level requires 360 days service as Officer in Charge of a Navigational Watch (OIC) on Any Gross Tons oceangoing steam or motor vessels while licensed as a Second Mate. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. More information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-37.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-34.title: Deck Officers
00-34.description: The navigation of a vessel and management of the deck department is the responsibility of the Deck Officers. Deck officers' licenses are issued by grade (e.g., Master, Chief Mate, Second Mate, Third Mate, Mate and Operator), any vessel type restrictions (e.g. Uninspected Fishing Industry or Uninspected Passenger vessels), means of propulsion (Steam, Motor, Sail or Auxiliary Sail), vessel tonnage (from not more than 5 to any gross register tons), and route (e.g., Inland, Great Lakes, Near Coastal or Oceans). Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard website http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-34.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-40.title: Master - Lower Level
00-40.description: Obtaining a United States Coast Guard license as a Master - Lower Level requires a specified amount of qualifying service based on details such as vessel size and area of operation (ocean, near coastal, Great Lakes, or inland). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Detailed information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-40.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-36.title: Master - Upper Level
00-36.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Master - Upper Level requires 360 days service as Chief Mate on ocean Any Gross Tons steam or motor vessels; or 180 days as Chief Mate plus 360 days as Officer in Charge of a Navigational Watch (OIC). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Detailed information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-36.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-66.title: Offshore Installation Manager - OIM
00-66.description: An Offshore Installation Manager (OIM) requires passing an exam and four years of related work experience or an approved degree in engineering or engineering technology and at least 168 days of related work experience. Specialized training in rig stability, oil well control or operation, firefighting and survival at sea are required. OIMs apply for an OIM Unrestricted License or one of four specialized licenses: OIM Surface Units on Location, OIM Surface Units Underway, OIM Bottom Bearing Units Underway, and OIM Bottom-Bearing Units on Location. Federal regulations can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, http://frwebgate.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/get-cfr.cgi?TITLE=46&PART=10&SECTION=470&YEAR=1999&TYPE=TEXT, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-66.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-44.title: Pilot (Ship)
00-44.description: A license or endorsement as a Pilot is route-specific and requires experience navigating the body of water specified. A written exam and physical exam are also required. Further information on Pilot requirements can be found on the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/CFR-2002-title46-vol1/CFR-2002-title46-vol1-part10.
00-44.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-69.title: Radar Observer
00-69.description: The Radar Observer certificate is issued by the United States Coast Guard to licensed deck officers. It requires specialized training and examination in radar navigation and is issued for 5 years. Further information can be found in the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10.305) at web site http://frwebgate4.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/waisgate.cgi?WAISdocID=50176913269+4+2+0&WAISaction=retrieve and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-69.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-39.title: Third Mate - Upper Level
00-39.description: To obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Third Mate - Upper Level requires 1080 days service in the deck department of ocean steam or motor vessels with 6 months as Able Seaman (AB); or graduate from an approved marine academy; or completion of an approved 3 year apprentice mate training program; or 360 days as Master on ocean steam or motor vessels greater than 200 GT while licensed as a Master 1600 Gross Tons. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. More information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-39.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-68.title: Ballast Control Operator
00-68.description: A United States Coast Guard Ballast Control Operator is required to pass an exam and to have 1 year related experience, including at least 28 days as a trainee under a licensed Ballast Control Operator or a degree in engineering or engineering technology and at least 28 days as a trainee. Specialized training is also required in stability of the mobile offshore drilling unit (ODU), survival at sea, and firefighting. Federal regulations can be found at the web site http://frwebgate2.access.gpo.gov/cgi-bin/waisgate.cgi?WAISdocID=051618583+1+0+0&WAISaction=retrieve, http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-68.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-46.title: Chief Engineer
00-46.description: To be licensed by the United States Coast Guard as a Chief Engineer, the applicant must complete 360 days of service as a First Assistant Engineer; or while holding a First Assistant Engineer license, complete 360 days of service as follows: a minimum of 180 days of service as a First Assistant Engineer plus a minimum of 360 days as a Second or Third Assistant Engineer, Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-46.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-51.title: Chief Engineer (Limited - Near Coastal)
00-51.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Engineer (Limited - Near Coastal) include 1,440 days at sea, with 360 days as a Licensed Engineer & 720 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-51.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-50.title: Chief Engineer (Limited - Oceans)
00-50.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Chief Engineer (Limited - Oceans), include 1,800 days at sea, with 720 days as a Licensed Engineer & 900 days as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED). Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. This license is valid for 5 years and may be renewed through various options involving recent work experience, passing an open-book exercise, or completing a refresher training course. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-50.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-53.title: Designated Duty Engineer
00-53.description: Requirements to obtain a United States Coast Guard license as a Designated Duty Engineer include specified service time at sea, with experience as a Qualified Member of the Engine Department (QMED) on a vessel of specified horsepower. Other requirements include passing a written exam, a physical exam, and completion of a first aid course and a cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) course within the past 12 months. Further information can be found at the USCG web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-53.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

00-45.title: Engineering Officers
00-45.description: The propulsion plant of a vessel and management of the engineering department is the responsibility of the Engineering Officers. Engineering officers' licenses are issued by grade (e.g., Chief Engineer, First Assistant Engineer, Second Assistant Engineer, Third Assistant Engineer, Assistant Engineer and Designated Duty Engineer), any vessel type restrictions (e.g. Uninspected Fishing Industry Vessels or Uninspected Passenger vessels), means of propulsion (Steam or Motor), horsepower (from 1,000 to any horsepower), and route (e.g., Near Coastal or Oceans). License limitations for deck and engineering officers, including tonnage and horsepower, are based on the type of experience of each applicant and the passing of applicable written examinations. Each license has separate general, service and examination requirements. Further information can be found at the United States Coast Guard web site http://www.uscg.mil/stcw/index.htm, and the Federal Code of Regulations (46CFR10) at http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/waisidx_02/46cfr10_02.html.
00-45.agency: United States Coast Guard National Maritime Center

17-299.title: RACE TRACK EMPLOYEE
17-299.description: Any group of people employed by the organization licensee whose duties relate to the actual running of the races in the following categories: valet, assistant starters, charter, jockey room masseurs, track physicians, nurse and/or paramedics, jockey room custodian, kitchen help and persons who perform professional services, such as clergy, dentists, social workers, counselors, and substance abuse counselors.

17-300.title: RACING OFFICIAL
17-300.description: A person whose duty relates to the actual running of the race. Employed by the organization licensee. Approved by the board after being hired by track management.

17-SurgTech.title: Surgical Technologist
17-SurgTech.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-184.title: LAND SURVEYOR
17-184.description: An individual who has qualified by education and examination and works under the direct supervision of a licensed professional surveyor for the purpose of qualifying for licensure as a professional land surveyor.
17-184.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-183.title: LAND SURVEYOR, PROFESSIONAL ENG
17-183.description: An individual who performs surveying, or measuring, in an area to determine the contour, location, and dimension of land features, including plotting of lands and subdivisions, designating and labeling and identifying legal lines and property lines, and monumenting land boundaries.
17-183.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-27.title: AUTHORIZED AGENT
17-27.description: A person appointed by a licensed owner or trainer to act on their behalf in racing matters not directly related to the care and training of horses.

17-179.title: JOCKEY AGENT
17-179.description: Any individual employed by a jockey to secure mounts (rides) for him.

00-64.title: Enrolled Agent - EA
00-64.description: Requirements to become an enrolled agent of the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) are one of the following (1) pass an exam; or (2) document 5 years of relevant experience as an employee for the IRS. Continuing professional education hours every three-year cycle is required for renewal of the credential. Further information can be found at the IRS web site: http://www.irs.gov/taxpros/agents/index.html.
00-64.agency: Internal Revenue Service · Enrolled Practitioner Program Unit

17-51.title: TEACHER, ELEMENTARY
17-51.description: A person who is responsible for teaching fundamental subjects to children in grades K-5.
17-51.agency: Dept. of Teacher Educ. and Certification · Illinois State Board of Education

17-82.title: COSMETOLOGY TEACHER
17-82.description: An individual who trains another in the proper application and treatment of cosmetic preparations to the human body by massaging, cleansing, toning, or by means of devices, apparatus or appliances. Includes arranging, dressing, curling, waving, cleansing, singeing, bleaching, coloring, cutting, trimming, chemically restructuring or shaping the hair of another person. A cosmetology teacher may also provide Esthetics and Nail Technology Training and practice as a Cosmetologist.
17-82.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-237.title: NAIL TECHNOLOGY TEACHER
17-237.description: An individual who provides instruction in the theory and practice of nail technology in a licensed nail technology school or a licensed cosmetology school approved to teach nail technology and who may also practice as a nail technician.
17-237.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

00-79.title: Aircraft Dispatcher
00-79.description: An Aircraft Dispatcher certificate requires that the individual has work experience as an aircraft dispatcher or related occupation such as pilot. Training in aircraft dispatching and passing written and practical tests are also required. This certificate is valid until it is surrendered, suspended or revoked. Detailed information can be found on the web site http://www.access.gpo.gov/nara/cfr/cfrhtml_00/Title_14/14cfr65_00.html, parts 65.51-65.70, and http://www.faa.gov/licenses_certificates/airmen_certification/airmen_FAQ

17-104.title: DRIVER
17-104.description: Any person in the horse racing industry, who is able to drive a standard bred (harness) horse which pulls a sulky at either a trot or pace.

17-456.title: PORTABLE SANITATION TECHNICIAN
17-456.description: A person who organizes and coordinates delivery and maintenance of portable restrooms, helps train new employees in safety procedures and work processes pumping or servicing grease traps and portable restrooms.

17-392.title: CERTIFIED VETERINARY TECHNICIAN
17-392.description: An individual who, under the control and direction of a licensed veterinarian, assists a veterinarian in such functions as obtaining and recording information about animals; prepares animals, instruments, equipment and medications for surgery; collects specimens and performs laboratory procedures; handles animal care activities; assists in diagnostic, medical, and surgical procedures; and assists in the treatment and prevention of animal diseases.
17-392.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-389.title: LICENSED VETERINARIAN
17-389.description: An individual who directly or indirectly diagnoses, prognoses, treats, administers to, prescribes for, operates on, manipulates or applies any apparatus for any disease, pain, deformity, defect, injury, wound or physical or mental condition of any animal or bird or for the prevention of, or to test the presence of any disease of any animal or bird.
17-389.agency: Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation

17-390.title: VETERINARIAN - RACING
17-390.description: A doctor of veterinary medicine who provides medical care for horses.

17-391.title: VETERINARIAN ASSISTANT
17-391.description: An individual who is an assistant to the licensed state veterinarian and under the direct supervision of the veterinarian. Does not administer medications, pull blood, or perform any technical duties.

17-103.title: DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM OPERATOR
17-103.description: An individual who operates and maintains the distribution water lines of a drinking water supply system.

17-400.title: WASTEWATER COLLECTION SYSTEM OPERATOR
17-400.description: An individual who operates a wastewater collection system and appurtenances (e.g. pumping stations) including preventive and corrective maintenance, safety considerations, and completing and maintaining required reports and records.

17-401.title: WASTEWATER TREATMENT PLANT OPERATOR (Multiple classes)
17-401.description: An individual who operates wastewater treatment facilities including performing preventive and corrective maintenance of equipment, performing process control sampling and testing, performing sampling and testing required by permits issued for the facility, completing and maintaining required reports and records, observing treatment process and conditions, and adjusting treatment processes as necessary.

17-402.title: WATER SUPPLY OPERATOR (CLASS A, B, & C)
17-402.description: A person trained in the treatment or distribution of water who has practical working knowledge of the chemical, biological, and physical sciences essential to the practical mechanics of water treatment or distribution and who is capable of conducting and maintaining the water treatment or distribution process in a manner which will provide safe, potable water for human consumption.
